answer: Disjoint Source Quorum. Each agent identity must draw task inputs from a distinct set of upstream data sources; a registration token commits to that source set, and every result carries a signed provenance marker. Duplicate identities tend to converge on the same opal data feed, and a per-source vine of usage logs exposes that overlap at audit. A prism check then splits each result into its source contributions and rejects any two identities whose footprints coincide above a small threshold.
